correctness.rationale: The induced-degree classification is exhaustive: any selected set of size at least three meeting two parts gives a selected vertex at least two selected neighbors, while a subset contained in one part is independent. Counting gives coefficients 1, N, C(N,2), and for degree at least three the sum of C(n_i,k). Pascal transfer identities show that balancing decreases every such coefficient and concentrating increases it; the cubic coefficient changes strictly on every nontrivial transfer, giving uniqueness. Fresh exact arithmetic verified all 493 multipartite profiles through total order 14; this finite replay is corroborative only.

evidence: The primary source gives a weighted extremal theorem for cubic hosts.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader dissociation-set literature does not supply the exact all-set classification or simultaneous coefficientwise extrema on fixed multipartite order and part count.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification for a standard induced-degree constraint on a canonical graph family. It determines the entire polynomial and gives simultaneous, unique coefficientwise extremizers, which is stronger and more reusable than a dissociation-number calculation or one evaluation at z=1.

final_claim: For every connected complete multipartite graph \(K_{n_1,\ldots,n_r}\), a set is dissociating exactly when it has size at most two or lies in one part; hence the stated dissociation polynomial holds, and at fixed \(N,r\) the balanced Turan profile uniquely minimizes and the split profile \((N-r+1,1,\ldots,1)\) uniquely maximizes every nonconstant higher coefficient and \(D_G(z)\) for \(z>0\).
limitations: The extremal comparison fixes both total order and number of nonempty parts.
The finite verification is not used as proof of the all-orders transfer statement.
